configuration: The single upstream case of unittest/geometry-object.cpp, test_clone, on one geometry object holding a sphere. The object's placement, the sphere's radius and the radius the case mutates the shape to are read from ic/<ic>/operands.json; upstream draws the placement from SE3::Random, which takes the unseeded std::rand stream inside the module a solver would port, and leaves the two radii as the literals 0.5 and 1.0, which would make every graded value insensitive to the variant. ic/nominal carries the two upstream literals unchanged. Graded: the placement of the object and of its clone, the radius of each before and after the mutation, and the local axis-aligned bounding box each shape computes for itself.
observable: the placement, shape radius and local bounding box a geometry object and its deep copy carry
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the placement and the two radii are initial conditions in ic/ rather than a random draw and two source literals
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero number of ic/nominal/operands.json; the zeros are left as they are, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is not a perturbation of a length, an angle or a quaternion coordinate. Perturbing every nonzero component rather than one component per quantity is deliberate: on an earlier Pinocchio leaf, moving a single entry of a rotation rounded away in an output built from all nine and left dozens of observables with a spread of exactly zero, while moving all of them is still a two-ulp calibration. Here that is the twelve numbers of the geometry placement and the two sphere radii. The placement is the only input the placement observables depend on and the radii are the only input the bounding boxes depend on, so both had to move for the calibration to reach every observable. All 13 numbers of ic/nominal/operands.json move; none of them is zero. The worst measured spread over all 64 graded values is 4.4409e-16 absolute.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. The graded quantities are rigid transform compositions and geometric distances between fixed shapes; Eigen fixes the evaluation order of the expressions, the loops are scalar, and coal's shape queries are closed form or an exhaustive minimum over a fixed set of features, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate. The alternative build was nevertheless run for every check of this leaf rather than assumed, because on an earlier Pinocchio leaf it was what exposed a graded buffer that was reading uninitialised memory.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned library, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantities are one geometry object's placement in its parent frame, in metres and in the object's own Cartesian axes, the radius of the sphere it carries, and the local axis-aligned bounding box that sphere computes, all of which the clone must reproduce exactly and none of which an implementation gets to reorder: the object is a single item, not a collection. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 1.00e+00, it admits about 1.01e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this case can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a clone that shared the shape instead of deep-copying it would report the mutated radius, a difference of 0.5 m, fifteen decades above the bound; a placement dropped or transposed on copy moves individual entries by order one; and the upstream equality assertions, which compare the clone against the original before and after the mutation, stay active as well, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these compositions differs by about a few units in the last place of the largest intermediate, some 1e-15 in these units, six decades inside the bound, and because the alternative build measured exactly zero. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value by 4.4409e-16, using 4.397e-07 of the bound, that is 2,274,318 times of headroom across all 64 graded values; and every graded value scaled by 0.1 per cent, a fault far smaller than any this test can express, is rejected at 990,099 times the bound. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
